Good, using the #clientops-main channel resolves the workspace anchoring issue without violating the no-name-lookup constraint. Now I need to check whether users.info actually returns a role field reflecting workspace membership, per the domain model spec.

The runtime qualifications confirm users.info exposes one workspace association per user, and owner/admin flags derive from the stored role - so the plan is documented and valid. Using conversations.members on #clientops-main followed by users.info calls on each member is a sound path, and Nora being the unique owner while Diego is admin and Felix is member confirms she's the correct unique target.

One assumption worth flagging: the plan implies Nora, Diego, and Felix are members of #clientops-main via conversations.members, even though this membership isn't explicitly stated in the role facts - it seems to be something the compiler will need to add as channel_members rows for these three plus the acting bot.

The identifying path still resolves through WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP->WORKSPACE matching team_id and role='owner'; the channel lookups are just how the actor discovers team_id, similar to using a visible ID to anchor traversal, so this fits the mechanical review criteria. I'm also confirming that conversations.members only returns user_ids while users.info determines role per user via the single-workspace-membership trick, which stays consistent with the runtime qualification.

Now I'm checking the rest of the design: answer_attributes (team_id, role, user_id) are all real columns, the DataOps guild members act as reasonable negative distractors, and the channel path referencing not-yet-seeded IDs is fine since it's just a design plan. The task itself is read-only rather than a write action, but that's acceptable for this query type, so overall the design looks valid and adequately specified.
